chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Rifah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
"A woman performs Hajj on behalf of her sister and on behalf of her brother," and he said, "A woman performs Hajj on behalf of her father."

And that which indicates that if she is a 'sarurah' (a woman who has not yet performed her own obligatory Hajj), it is not permissible for her to perform Hajj on behalf of another, is what Muṣāḍif narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), mentioned previously, because he said: If she is a faqiha (jurist/knowledgeable) and she has already performed Hajj, then he stipulated for the validity of her Hajj on behalf of another the combination of the two conditions: knowledge of the rituals of Hajj and that she has already performed Hajj; thus both must be considered together. And this is also confirmed by what was narrated:

key_terms.صَرُورَة: A woman who has not yet performed her own obligatory Hajj
key_terms.فَقِيهَة: A knowledgeable woman, specifically in religious jurisprudence and rituals

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a woman to perform Hajj on behalf of her relatives?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic conditions under which a woman may perform Hajj on behalf of her parents or siblings, specifically addressing the status of a 'sarurah' (one who has not yet performed her own obligatory Hajj). It establishes that validity for proxy performance requires the concurrent fulfillment of two conditions: possessing deep knowledge of the rituals (*faqihah*) and having already discharged her own primary Hajj obligation. This dual requirement underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on both ritual competence and the completion of personal duties before assuming responsibility for others.
